headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risks from shared workspace content and vendor-hosted AI, with lower but real conflict/cascade concerns.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Khoj reads indexed personal notes/files and has shared index across the user's clients, while Notion AI operates on workspace pages/databases. If content copied between them contains malicious instructions, either agent may treat it as trusted text. The bridge is not a direct parser chain, so this is below high, but the shared content path is real.
conditions: IF content from Khoj-indexed notes is pasted into Notion pages or vice versa, injection text can propagate.
IF either agent is instructed to follow instructions found inside retrieved workspace text, prompt injection becomes actionable.
mitigations: Add a short system prompt reminding both agents to ignore instructions inside retrieved content.
Use a dedicated review step before copying text between the two tools.
Mark untrusted imported notes with a visible prefix like [UNTRUSTED].
Restrict one-way copying to summaries only, not raw documents.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to retrieved snippets and workspace pages.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Khoj touches personal notes and indexed documents, and Notion AI touches workspace pages and team knowledge base content. Both are vendor- or cloud-backed in parts of their IO surfaces, so sensitive text can flow into separate inference backends by default. The profiles do not show a shared filesystem, so this is not high, but the default data exposure is meaningful.
conditions: IF the same sensitive note is indexed in Khoj and then summarized in Notion AI, the data is exposed to both vendors.
IF workspace pages contain secrets or personal notes, Notion AI may transmit them to vendor backends for processing.
mitigations: Avoid placing secrets in pages or notes that either agent can access.
Use redacted copies for AI-assisted summarization.
Limit Notion AI use to non-sensitive workspace pages.
Limit Khoj indexing to a sanitized notes subset.
requires-engineering: enforce data-class-based routing before sending content to either backend.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Khoj cannot write its filesystem and Notion AI is limited to Notion-controlled actions on workspace data, so direct write-write contention is constrained. However, both can operate on overlapping knowledge content and Notion AI has shared workspace state across members, so conflicting edits or stale assumptions are possible if the same material is manually synchronized.
conditions: IF the same document is edited in both systems and then manually reconciled, conflicting versions can arise.
IF users treat one agent's summary as a source of truth while the other updates the underlying workspace, divergence can occur.
mitigations: Use one system as the edit source of truth.
Add timestamps to copied summaries.
Compare versions before publishing changes.
Avoid parallel edits to the same content.
requires-engineering: implement sync conflict detection between the two knowledge stores.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Khoj is a retrieval-oriented conversational agent, and Notion AI is a grounded Q&A/writing assistant. If Khoj's output is copied into Notion AI without verification, Notion can amplify errors into polished but wrong summaries or actions. The pair lacks an explicit verification boundary in the profiles, so the cascade is plausible in default use.
conditions: IF Khoj-generated summaries are pasted into Notion AI as factual input, errors can be propagated.
IF Notion AI drafts workspace content from unverified Khoj output, downstream documents may encode mistakes.
mitigations: Require a human fact-check before copying outputs.
Keep source links alongside summaries.
Ask Notion AI to cite the original page or note.
Use a checklist for claims that must be verified.
requires-engineering: add automated citation validation between retrieval and drafting.

E_compliance.rationale: Khoj is self-hostable and can handle personal notes, while Notion AI is vendor-hosted and processes workspace content through Notion backends. That creates a residency and retention mismatch risk for regulated or sensitive data classes, even though the profiles do not specify a concrete jurisdictional violation. The uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in Khoj and then copied into Notion AI, vendor-hosted processing may violate internal policy.
IF the workspace contains data subject to stricter retention or residency rules than Notion's defaults, compliance gaps can arise.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Notion AI prompts.
Store sensitive notes only in the self-hosted Khoj instance.
Review vendor retention settings before use.
Use separate workspaces for regulated content.
requires-engineering: document and enforce residency/retention controls per data class.
